answer: Trust can be aged into an identity: a fresh account starts with negligible voting weight that grows slowly with verified uptime, so a sybil farmer gains nothing by spawning clones today, and waiting buys no shortcut. Each new agent must also collect attestations from peers spread across the network rather than its own neighborhood, so clones vouching for clones wander nowhere; their trust graph stays a tight clump the protocol can discount. The cost falls on the attacker like ferrous weight on a balloon, while honest agents climb the trellis of earned attestation at their own pace.
